query: What is the current status of SpaceX Starship Flight 13 (IFT-13) as of mid-July 2026? Has Booster 20 completed its static fire test? Has the FAA approved Flight 13 / accepted the Flight 12 mishap investigation? What is the latest NET (no earlier than) launch date shown on trackers like NextSpaceflight and RGV Aerial Photography?
answer:
I've completed the research. Here's the key takeaway:

**The premise of the question is outdated.** As of the current date (July 27, 2026), all the milestones asked about have been resolved and **Flight 13 has already launched successfully:**

- **Booster 20 static fire:** ✅ Completed July 10, 2026 (33-engine, ~25-second firing — longest Super Heavy static fire to date)
- **FAA approval / Flight 12 mishap investigation:** ✅ FAA closed the Flight 12 investigation on July 13, 2026, accepting SpaceX's corrective actions and clearing Flight 13
- **Launch date (NET):** Superseded by events — targeted July 16 (aborted at T-0 on Raptor turbo-pump issues), scrubbed July 23 for weather, then **launched July 24, 2026** at 6:51 p.m. EDT

**Outcome:** First flight of Starship V3; deployed 20 operational Starlink V3 satellites (first Starship flight to deploy operational satellites); Ship 40 soft splashdown in the Indian Ocean; Booster 20 had a hard splashdown after only ~10 of 13 engines relit during its landing burn.

Full details, sources, and structured data points have been recorded via the StructuredOutput tool.

key_facts: Starship Flight 13 (IFT-13) already launched successfully on July 24, 2026, at 6:51 p.m. EDT from Starbase, Texas — the question's premise that it was pending is outdated.
Flight 13 used Booster 20 (Super Heavy V3) and Ship 40; it was the first flight of Starship Version 3 (V3).

Booster 20 completed a full-duration 33-engine static fire on July 10, 2026, lasting roughly 25 seconds — the longest Super Heavy static fire to date. Preceded by cryogenic proof testing in June 2026.
The FAA closed its Flight 12 mishap investigation on July 13, 2026, accepting SpaceX's findings/corrective actions and clearing Flight 13 (no public injury or property damage reported).
Flight 12 launched May 22, 2026; the FAA had required a SpaceX-led mishap investigation before Starship flights could resume (determination made ~May 27, 2026).
First launch attempt on July 16, 2026 aborted automatically at T-0 due to six Raptor engines having oxidizer turbo-pump problems.
A July 23 attempt was scrubbed for weather (Tropical Storm Bertha / heat-shield imagery visibility) and postponed one day to July 24.
Flight 13 was the first Starship flight to deploy operational satellites: 20 Starlink V3 satellites deployed suborbitally, which made contact with ground receivers.
Ship 40 completed a successful reentry and soft splashdown in the Indian Ocean (reported as softest splashdown achieved).
Booster 20 suffered a partial landing-burn failure — only about 10 of 13 planned Raptor engines relit and two shut off within seconds — resulting in a hard splashdown.
